data.title: Balance Scale Meanings
data.description: Answer out loud to practice what the equal sign means using balance scales.

input.objectiveText: Explain what the equal sign means using the balance scale example
input.intent: Engage students with a live tutor asking spoken-response questions that prompt them to say aloud what '=' means ('same as' or 'balanced') when looking at various scale images.

data.title: Scale Balance Meanings
data.description: You will answer out loud to explain what the equal sign means.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means the same as or balanced.
items.ask: Four plus one equals five. What does the equal sign tell us about these two sides?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any phrasing that clearly describes the two sides matching, weighing the same, or being equal counts as correct.
items.signatureError: Saying just the sum, five, is not an explanation of what the equal sign means.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means that both sides are the same as each other. Four plus one is the same as five.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means the same as or balanced.
items.ask: Three equals three. When you look at the scale, what is the meaning of the equal sign here?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any words that say the sides are even or match each other count as the correct idea.
items.signatureError: Repeating the number three back as an explanation is not correct.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign shows that the scale is balanced because three is the same as three.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means the same as or balanced.
items.ask: Five equals two plus three. What does the equal sign tell us about the left and right sides?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any wording showing that the two sides match or are equal counts.
items.signatureError: Naming just one of the numbers on the right side is not an explanation.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign tells us that five is the same as two plus three, keeping the scale balanced.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means the same as or balanced.
items.ask: Six equals six. What is the rule that the equal sign shows us on the scale?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any clear statement that the sides are even, equal, or the same counts.
items.signatureError: Saying the number six without explaining the sign is not correct.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign shows that both sides are balanced because six is the same as six.

data.title: Balanced Scales and Equal Signs
data.description: You will answer out loud to explain what the equal sign means using balance scales.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means both sides are balanced.
items.ask: Three plus two equals five. What does the equal sign mean in this number sentence?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any words that clearly say the two sides are equal, even, or match each other count as a right answer.
items.signatureError: Saying the total number five is not an explanation of what the equal sign means.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means both sides are balanced and hold the exact same amount. Three plus two is the same as five.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means both sides are balanced.
items.ask: Four equals one plus three. Tell what the equal sign tells us about these two sides.
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any words that clearly state the two sides are equal, even, or match count as right.
items.signatureError: Saying just the number four or three is not an explanation.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means both sides are balanced and hold the same value. Four is the same as one plus three.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means both sides are balanced.
items.ask: Six equals six. What does the equal sign mean when you look at both sides?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any response describing the sides as matching, even, or balanced is correct.
items.signatureError: Just repeating the number six back without explaining the sign is not correct.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means both sides are balanced and have the same amount.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means both sides are balanced.
items.ask: Two plus four equals three plus three. What does the equal sign tell us about the two sides?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any phrasing showing that the left side and right side are equal or balanced counts.
items.signatureError: Saying that the answer comes next or pointing out the plus sign is not correct.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means both sides are balanced and weigh the exact same amount.

data.title: Pattern Rules
data.description: Practice explaining pattern rules out loud with the voice tutor.

items.conceptStatement: This number pattern grows by adding two each time.
items.ask: Two, four, six, eight. What is the rule of this pattern?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any words that clearly mean counting by twos or adding two count as the answer.
items.signatureError: Saying the next number, ten, is not the rule.
items.correctionBody: The rule is plus two. Each number grows by adding two more.

items.conceptStatement: This pattern grows by adding five each time.
items.ask: Five, ten, fifteen, twenty. What is the rule of this pattern?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any phrasing that describes counting by fives counts as the answer.
items.signatureError: Saying twenty-five is not the rule.
items.correctionBody: The rule is plus five. Each step goes up by five.

items.conceptStatement: This pattern grows by adding three each time.
items.ask: Three, six, nine, twelve. What is the growing rule for this numbers pattern?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any words that describe adding three or counting by threes count as correct.
items.signatureError: Saying the next number fifteen is NOT the rule.
items.correctionBody: The rule is plus three. The numbers increase by three each time.

items.conceptStatement: This size pattern repeats big then small over and over.

items.signatureError: Saying just one size word is not an explanation of the pattern rule.
items.correctionBody: The rule is big then small. The sizes repeat in that exact order.

items.conceptStatement: This pattern grows by adding two each time.

items.signatureError: Saying the next number in the pattern, ten, is NOT an explanation of the rule.
items.correctionBody: The rule is plus two. The numbers go up by two every time.

items.conceptStatement: This pattern grows by adding five each time.
items.ask: Five, ten, fifteen, twenty. What is the secret rule here?

items.acceptRule: Any words describing counting by fives count as the answer.
items.signatureError: Saying the next number, twenty-five, is NOT an explanation of the rule.
items.correctionBody: The rule is plus five. Each number gets five more added to it.
